question: What is the main superpower of community herd immunity?

options.A: Reducing the cost of hospital building construction
options.B: Protecting vulnerable individuals who cannot be vaccinated
options.C: Eliminating the need for clean water and sanitation
options.D: Ensuring every adult receives an annual booster shot

explanation: When most people around are immunized, it builds a protective shield around babies or sick individuals who cannot take vaccines yet. Brilliant concept to master! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h1)

question: Why do community health nurses need to adjust their standard routines during village outreach?

options.A: Government policies prohibit giving injections outside of clinics
options.B: Field conditions and local environments vary greatly compared to hospitals
options.C: Community members refuse standard hospital documentation forms
options.D: Vaccines given outdoors lose their chemical composition entirely

explanation: Outreach doesn't have the fancy setup of a hospital ward, so nurses get creative to keep things safe and sterile outside! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h1)

question: What happens when a vaccine gets too warm because the cold chain broke?

options.A: It expires in exactly one hour
options.C: It turns a bright neon color
options.D: It becomes safe to ingest orally

explanation: Heat damage can't be undone! Once a vaccine gets too warm, it won't protect the patient anymore, which is why keeping things cold is top priority. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h2)

question: Why must nurses condition ice packs before putting them in a daily vaccine carrier?

options.A: To prevent the accidental freezing of freeze-sensitive vaccines
options.B: To ensure the ice melts faster during the hot afternoon sun
options.C: To make the vaccine carrier lighter for the nurse to carry
options.D: To activate the chemical VVM label on the vaccine vials

explanation: Direct contact with rock-solid ice can freeze and ruin liquid vaccines like tetanus. Conditioning the ice keeps the temperature just right! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h2)

question: Which of these is a true red-light contraindication for giving a vaccine?

options.A: A history of severe allergic reaction to a previous dose
options.B: A mild cold with a low-grade fever of 37.8 degrees
options.C: A family history of minor skin rashes
options.D: Current recovery from mild diarrhea at home

explanation: If a patient had a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) before, giving another dose is a huge safety risk. Always check past records! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h3)

question: A mother brings her baby for immunization, but the child has a mild runny nose. What should you do?

options.A: Send the child home until all cold symptoms completely disappear
options.B: Refer the child immediately to the main district hospital
options.C: Give half the normal dose because the immune system is busy
options.D: Proceed with the vaccination as minor illness is not a contraindication

explanation: A little sniffle or low fever shouldn't stop life-saving vaccines! Minor illnesses don't block the immune response. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h3)

question: At what angle do you insert the needle for an intramuscular (IM) injection?
explanation: Straight down! A 90-degree angle ensures the needle punches right through the skin into the deep muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h4)

question: A nurse is getting ready to give a newborn the BCG vaccine. Which technique and site are correct?

options.A: Subcutaneous injection in the fatty abdominal tissue
options.B: Oral drops placed directly onto the infant tongue
options.C: Intramuscular injection in the anterolateral thigh
options.D: Intradermal injection on the upper left arm

explanation: BCG goes right into the upper layer of the skin (intradermally) on the arm, leaving a cute little raised bump! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h4)

question: Why chat with local community leaders before holding an immunization outreach in their village?

options.A: To ensure the nurse receives financial compensation from the village
options.B: To let the leaders handle the actual administration of injections
options.C: To build trust and reduce resistance or hesitancy among residents
options.D: To bypass government regulations regarding cold chain transport

explanation: Community leaders have the people's ear. Working with them helps families feel safe and excited about getting vaccinated. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h5)

question: How long should patients wait at the clinic after getting an immunization?

options.C: Until the end of the market day

explanation: That 15-minute window is a crucial safety check just in case a rare allergic reaction pops up right away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h5)

question: In community health nursing, what does the term AEFI stand for?
explanation: AEFI is simply any health issue that happens after a vaccine, whether the vaccine caused it or not. Good term to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h6)

question: Which of these is a serious AEFI that needs urgent reporting?

options.A: A low-grade fever lasting for less than one day
options.B: A severe allergic reaction with difficulty breathing
options.C: Mild drowsiness after receiving multiple vaccines
options.D: Mild redness and soreness at the injection site

explanation: Breathing trouble is a red flag requiring immediate medical care and official reporting to keep immunization safe for everyone. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h6)

question: What is the main use of tally sheets during a busy immunization outreach?

options.A: To serve as the child's permanent health card kept at home
options.B: To calculate the total financial cost of running the clinic
options.C: To quickly record each dose given using tick marks without slowing down
options.D: To track the exact temperature of the vaccine carrier

explanation: Tally sheets are a nurse's best friend in a busy crowd—just quick tick marks to keep an accurate count while saving time! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h7)

question: Why is the home-based child health card such a lifesaver in immunization programs?

options.A: It automatically orders new vaccine supplies from the central store
options.B: It replaces the need for nurses to keep facility registers
options.C: It acts as a legal permit for children to enter primary school
options.D: It provides a portable, lifelong record that travels with the child

explanation: Parents keep it safe at home and bring it along, meaning any nurse anywhere can instantly see what vaccines the child has received! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h7)
